3. If $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$ then all three identities of claim 1 hold for all $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\eta\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. For
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$, suppose that for every $\gamma\le\alpha$ there is
$v_\gamma\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$D^\gamma u=v_\gamma$ weakly. Then $\eta u$ has a weak $\alpha$-derivative,
and its almost-everywhere class is
$$D^\alpha(\eta u)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}(D^\beta\eta)D^{\alpha-\beta}u\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
where $D^\beta\eta$ is the classical derivative and products are pointwise
products of representatives. The resulting class does not depend on the
representatives.

For $k\in\mathbb N_0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, if
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and $D^\beta\eta\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ for
every $|\beta|\le k$, then $\eta u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and the same
formula holds in $L^p$ for every $|\alpha|\le k$. In particular,
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is a sufficient condition on the
multiplier for this global conclusion.

For $\Omega=\varnothing$ all classes are zero and the identity holds. The
pairing convention is bilinear, with no complex conjugation.

supplier_inspections.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), $c>0$, and fix $k\ge2$. Let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ and let $\chi$ be a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). Then the gauge transform $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+
abla\chi)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and its field pair is the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$: $$E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\qquad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I,$$ the common value being a map $\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly (the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$ in the sense of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). In particular, gauge related potential representations of a field pair ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]) have equal field pairs: the electric and magnetic fields are gauge invariants of the framework, and no value of $\varphi$, $A$ or $\chi$ is asserted to be observable. The identity uses only the definitions $E=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, the vanishing of $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi$ for the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the equality of the mixed partials $\partial_t\partial_i\chi=\partial_i\partial_t\chi$; no Maxwell equation, no hypothesis on $\Omega$ beyond openness and no choice principle is used.
supplier_inspections.strategy:
Magnetic field: $\operatorname{curl}(A+
abla\chi)=\operatorname{curl}A+\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=\operatorname{curl}A$ by linearity of the curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]) and $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=0$ ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], applicable because $\chi$ is $C^2$, indeed $C^k$ with $k\ge2$). Electric field: componentwise, $-
abla(\varphi-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(A+
abla\chi)=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA+(
abla\partial_t\chi-\partial_t
abla\chi)$, where the bracket vanishes by equality of the mixed second partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the componentwise linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ is [[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Regularity: $\partial_t\chi$ and $
abla\chi$ are $C^{k-1}$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so the transformed pair is $C^{k-1}$ and the two displayed field expressions are legitimate there; the common value equals the $C^{k-1}$ map $E(\varphi,A)$, resp. $B(\varphi,A)$, supplied by [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. No further hypothesis is used.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega\times I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,\rho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+\nabla G=\mu_0J\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega\times I$. (c) [Decoupling] For this pair and sources, the pair is in Lorenz gauge and satisfies the two decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$ if and only if its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system on $\Omega\times I$ (the source-free pair $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ being automatic for a potential pair). Thus in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system is exactly a pair of decoupled wave equations, componentwise for $A$. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.
supplier_inspections.strategy:
(a) Componentwise expansion using the sum rules for divergence and curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), the vector identity $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (b) Direct expansion of $T_\chi$: $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{div}A+\Delta\chi+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G-W\chi$, using linearity and the $C^2$ mixed-partials identity for $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the field part is [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. (c) is the combination of (a) and (b) with the automatic source-free pair; (d) is (b) with $G=0$ and $W\chi=0$. All statements are pointwise on $\Omega	imes I$; the constants $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ are those of the framework postulates ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]). No choice principle, no hypothesis on the shape of $\Omega$ and no solvability of $W\chi=G$ is used.

supplier_inspections.statement: Let $c>0$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-em-fields]]) satisfying the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on $\Omega\times I$ in their pointwise form $$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]) with $$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ If $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen of class $C^\infty$ jointly. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $(E,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open $\Omega$, no boundary or decay condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness; potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and not claimed to be observable.

supplier_inspections.statement_read:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$, let
$\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$. Suppose $f$ and $g$ are continuous at
$c$ ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then:

1. $f + g$, $\alpha f$ and $fg$ are continuous at $c$;
2. $|f|$, the function $x \mapsto |f(x)|$, is continuous at $c$;
3. $\max\{f,g\}$ and $\min\{f,g\}$, defined pointwise by
   $x \mapsto \max\{f(x), g(x)\}$ and $x \mapsto \min\{f(x), g(x)\}$
   ([[def-max-min]]), are continuous at $c$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is continuous at
   $c$ as a function on $A_0$.

Moreover, with no hypothesis at all:

5. every constant function $A \to \mathbb{R}$ and the identity
   $\mathrm{id} : A \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto x$, are continuous on $A$; hence
   so is $x \mapsto x^{n}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$
   ([[def-integer-power]]), and hence so is every **polynomial function**
   $x \mapsto a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^{n}$ with real coefficients.

Consequently, if $f$ and $g$ are continuous **on** $A$ then so are $f+g$,
$\alpha f$, $fg$, $|f|$, $\max\{f,g\}$ and $\min\{f,g\}$, and
$(f/g)|_{A_0}$ is continuous on $A_0$.

**Claim 4 is stated on $A_0$ because $f/g$ is not defined where $g$ vanishes**,
and $g$ may well vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$. The hypothesis is
$g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ nowhere zero"; what it buys is that $c$ itself lies in
the smaller domain, which is what makes continuity there mean anything.

**Nothing here is proved through a sequence.** Claims 1 and 4 are read off from
[[thm-algebra-of-function-limits]], which is itself proved from $\varepsilon$
and $\delta$, and claims 2, 3 and 5 are proved directly below. So no choice
principle is used anywhere in this item.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$
If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then $\partial_i\partial_j f=\partial_j\partial_i f$ for every pair of coordinate indices.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$;
write $\delta_hu=(\delta_h^1u,\dots,\delta_h^nu)$ and
$Du=(D_1u,\dots,D_nu)$ for the difference-quotient and gradient vectors, with
$$\|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|\delta_h^iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega')},\qquad \|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|D_iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
(1) If $1\le p\le\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, then for every
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)$ and every coordinate
direction $i$,
$$\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le n^{|1/p-1/2|}\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
At $p=2$ the vector estimate has constant one. The coordinate bound also
holds on any open $U\subseteq\Omega$ for a fixed $i,h$ for which every
segment $[x,x+he_i]$, $x\in U$, stays in $\Omega$; compact containment
is unnecessary. In particular, $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(H)}\le
\|D_iu\|_{L^p(H)}$ for tangential directions on a half-space $H$.
(2) Conversely, if $1<p<\infty$, $u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and there is $C$
with $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$ for every coordinate $i$ and all
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)/2$, then
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega')$ with $D_iu\in L^p(\Omega')$,
$\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$, and
$\delta_h^iu\rightharpoonup D_iu$ weakly in $L^p(\Omega')$ as $h\to0$.
For $1\le p<\infty$, tangential quotients on $H$ also converge strongly:
$\delta_h^iu\to D_iu$ in $L^p(H)$ as $h\to0$.
Both parts are identities of classes and hold without any regularity of
$\partial\Omega$. At $p=1$ the converse in (2) is deliberately not asserted;
the companion remark records why only a measure derivative survives there.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge2$, a bounded $C^1$ domain Omega and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$. Both integrals are finite, with the continuous interior derivative convention and the outward normal on every boundary component.

supplier_inspections.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability lemmas. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] is the local graph definition used throughout), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive ($\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ on $\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$), and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. Then:
(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ pointwise with $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.
(b) **Neumann.** For every smooth outward conormal datum $g$ satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$, there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$. It is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ for each component gives a unique normalised solution, smooth on each closed component. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$, with a single additive constant.
(c) **Transmission.** For the stated finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth bulk $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b). The weak right-hand side includes $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$ and, in the Neumann case, $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique. With outer Neumann data it exists exactly when the total right-hand side vanishes on the constant of each connected component, equivalently $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for each $j$, and is unique modulo componentwise constants; zero componentwise means give uniqueness. In either case the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]].
Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this item states the combined existence-and-regularity theorem on the declared domains.
supplier_inspections.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Testing the displayed weak identity with the constant on each component gives $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, including the minus sign when solved for the outer conormal integral. Necessity of componentwise compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) Apply the transmission functional including the sheet-charge term, with outer Dirichlet tests in $H_0^1$ for full uniqueness, or outer Neumann tests in $H^1$ with that functional zero on every componentwise constant and the chosen mean normalisation. The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.

supplier_inspections.statement_read:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then for every open set
$V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ there is a bounded
linear extension operator
$$E:W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad (Eu)|_\Omega=u\ \text{a.e. on }\Omega,$$
such that $\operatorname{supp}(Eu)$ is a compact subset of $V$ for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. In particular each bounded $C^k$ domain is a
$W^{k,p}$-extension domain, with an operator whose output is supported in any
prescribed neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$. For $k=0$, extension by zero
is an isometric $L^p$ extension on any open $\Omega$; its output is supported
in the compact set $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ when $\Omega$ is bounded.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable
([[def-darboux-integral]]), let $F$ be its integral function
([[def-the-integral-function]]), and let $c \in [a,b]$ be a point at which $f$ is
continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $F$ is differentiable at $c$ as a
function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]) and

$$F'(c) \;=\; f(c) .$$

At $c = a$ and $c = b$ this is the one-sided statement, which is what
[[def-derivative]] means at those points: every point of a nondegenerate interval
is a limit point of it, so $F'(c)$ is a meaningful symbol at every $c \in [a,b]$,
and the difference quotient is taken over $[a,b] \setminus \{c\}$.

**Consequently, if $f$ is continuous on the whole of $[a,b]$, then $F$ is a
primitive of $f$ there**: $F' = f$ at every point of $[a,b]$.

**Continuity at $c$ is a hypothesis and it cannot be dropped.** For an integrable
$f$ that is discontinuous at $c$, $F'(c)$ may fail to exist, and it may exist and
differ from $f(c)$; both are exhibited on the companion page, by
an integrable function with no primitive and by a false
statement about the integral function.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Let $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $r^k$ be the integer power ([[def-integer-power]]),
so that $r^0 = 1$ for every $r$, including $r = 0$.

1. If $|r| < 1$ then the series $\sum r^k$ converges ([[def-series]]) and
   $$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^{k} \;=\; \frac{1}{1-r} .$$
2. If $|r| \ge 1$ then $\sum r^k$ diverges.

The series starts at $k = 0$ and its first term is $r^0 = 1$; in particular
$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} 2^{-k} = 2$, while the series starting at $k = 1$ sums to
$1$. Which starting index is meant has to be said, and it is said here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded
$C^{k+2}$ domain, $n\ge2$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$k\ge0$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega)$, $b^i,c\in W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ and all
coefficient derivatives bounded, and let $f\in H^k(\Omega)$. If
$u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of $Lu=f$ with zero boundary values
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^{k+2}(\Omega)$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}(\Omega)}\le C\big(\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\big),$$
with $C$ depending only on $n,k,\Omega$ and the coefficient bounds. The
derivative gain is exactly two orders; the boundary regularity required at
order $k$ is $C^{k+2}$, the coefficient regularity one order above the data
order, and the companion page records the sharp two-derivative example. For
$k=0$ the theorem is
[[thm-global-h-two-dirichlet-regularity]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\partial\Omega$ carry the
chart-independent surface measure of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and
[[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]], let
$1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then there is a
unique bounded linear operator
$$T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow L^p(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $Tu=u|_{\partial\Omega}$ for every
$u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and it satisfies
$\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. On each
boundary chart the operator is the flat half-space trace of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]] transported by the flattening
diffeomorphism, and the chartwise definitions agree on overlaps; uniqueness
holds because two bounded operators agreeing on the dense subspace
$C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ are equal.

Let $(x_k)$ be a sequence of reals ([[def-sequence]]) and let
$S = \{x_k : k \in \mathbb{N}\}$ be its range.

1. If $(x_k)$ is nondecreasing ([[def-monotone-sequence]]) and $S$ is bounded
   above ([[def-bounded-set]]), then $(x_k)$ converges ([[def-real-limit]]) and
   $$\lim_{k} x_k = \sup S .$$
2. If $(x_k)$ is nonincreasing and $S$ is bounded below, then $(x_k)$ converges
   and $$\lim_{k} x_k = \inf S .$$

Both suprema and infima exist under the stated hypotheses: $S$ is nonempty, so
the least-upper-bound property ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) supplies the
first and [[thm-infimum-property]] the second, and each is unique
([[lem-sup-unique]]).

This is the first place in this track where the least-upper-bound property
produces a **limit**. Everything on the sequences page held in any Archimedean
ordered field; the theorem below does not, and the sequence of decimal
truncations of $\sqrt 2$ inside $\mathbb{Q}$ is the standard witness of its
failure there.

A nonzero real polynomial of degree $n$ has at most $n$ distinct real roots. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-real-polynomial-degree-leading-coefficient-and-monic]], [[lem-real-polynomial-factor-at-a-root]], [[thm-induction-principle]].

Assume countable choice (in particular, the Axiom of Choice suffices). Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $1\le p\le\infty$. Then
$L^p(\mu)$, with the norm of
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]], is
complete. Equivalently, the metric induced by that norm is a complete metric in
the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]].

Moreover, if a sequence in $L^p(\mu)$ converges in norm, then some subsequence
admits measurable representatives converging almost everywhere in the sense of
[[def-convergence-almost-everywhere-relative-to-a-measure]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let $f$ be a bounded linear functional on $H$ ([[def-dual-space-of-a-normed-space]]). Then there is a unique $y\in H$ with

$$f(x)=\langle x,y\rangle\qquad\text{for every }x\in H,$$

and $\|f\|=\|y\|$, where $\|f\|$ is the dual norm ([[def-operator-norm]]). Under the first-variable-linear convention the representing vector depends conjugate-linearly and isometrically on $f$: if $f_i$ is represented by $y_i$ and $a,b$ are scalars, then $af_1+bf_2$ is represented by $\overline a\,y_1+\overline b\,y_2$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and $n\ge1$. In the proof write $e_n$
for the last canonical basis vector $e_{n-1}$. Let
$H=\mathbb R^{n-1}\times(0,\infty)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be the upper
half-space, written $x=(x',t)$ with $x'\in\mathbb R^{n-1}$ and $t>0$. For every
$k\in\mathbb N_0$, every $1\le p\le\infty$ and every
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ there is a bounded linear extension
operator
$$E_{k,p}:W^{k,p}(H;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad (E_{k,p}u)|_H=u\ \text{almost everywhere on }H .$$
For $k\ge1$ one may take, with the unique coefficients
$(a_1,\dots,a_k)\in\mathbb R^k$ satisfying
$\sum_{j=1}^k a_j(-j)^m=1$ for $m=0,1,\dots,k-1$,
$$E_{k,p}u(x',t)=u(x',t)\ \ (t>0),\qquad E_{k,p}u(x',t)=\sum_{j=1}^k a_ju(x',-jt)\ \ (t<0),$$
and for $k=0$ one may take the even reflection
$E_{0,p}u(x',t)=u(x',|t|)$. In particular $H$ is a $W^{k,p}$-extension
domain in the sense of [[def-sobolev-extension-domain-and-extension-operator]]
for every $k$ and every $p$, and no density assertion is made or needed.
